newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTIKO EYES LITHUANIA, UKRAINE MKTS.
newsitem.headline: ESTIKO EYES LITHUANIA, UKRAINE MKTS.

text.p: Packaging and plastics firm Estiko said on Wednesday that it was hoping for more business from sales in Lithuania and Ukraine but was being careful over plans for the Ukrainian market.
"Our greatest hopes are for better connections to Lithuania and Ukraine," Estiko chairman Kellju Hellenurm told Reuters in an interview.
"Sales to Lithuania could increase by five to seven percent, this is around 2 to 3 million kroons," he added.
He also said he had recently visited Ukraine.
"In Ukraine there are very many buyers but not very many payers so we are carefully chossing those who pay in advance," Hellenurm said.
"Our main products will be packaging materials for the food industry. More concretely, we have been selling bags of various sizes for Ukrainian sugar," he added.
He said there was one person working for Estiko in Ukraine at the moment, doing market research.
"But under Ukrainian law we need to establish a joint venture, we hope that this will happen," he said.
"It was just my first visit, I do not think it will happen very quickly," he added.
"We expect that by the end of 1997 two percent of our sales will be to Ukraine," he said.

Hellenurm also said that the company was gradually decreasing the number of its 9 subsidiaries, which it formed when it first began business in 1991 as there was other way to get the services it needed.
"Over the last year and during the next year about seven of the subsidiaries have either been sold or will be sold," he said.
He also said that company's planned share issue would be used mainly to fund a new 12-floor office building in Tartu, which will have office and retail space.
"We do not expect returns for 8 to 10 years on the project," he added.
